1.summary: LiveStateStore now supports terminal-run retention: mark_terminal moves a run out of the live map into a bounded 100-entry completed ring (with workflow_type/created_at/updated_at/terminal flag via get_record), while get()/list_active()/record()/remove() keep their original signatures and semantics.
decisions: Kept record(run_id, snapshot) and get(run_id) signatures byte-identical to avoid breaking http.rs/abort.rs/bastion callers outside this task's file scope; added mark_terminal and get_record as sibling entry points instead of overloading record.

get() now checks the live map first, then falls back to the completed ring, so it keeps serving a snapshot for terminal runs too (matches the task's explicit unit-test requirement) while list_active() only reads the live map so terminal runs are excluded.

mark_terminal takes the snapshot as an explicit parameter (not implicitly read from the live map) so the caller controls exactly what gets retained and the call doesn't depend on record() having been invoked first.

2.summary: POST /events/ now spawns the run via actix_web::rt::spawn and returns 202 {run_id, event_id} immediately (event_id == run_id), seeded with a default Budget read from ENGINE_RUN_MAX_COST_USD/ENGINE_RUN_MAX_TOKENS via a memoized OnceLock helper, with the spawned task marking the run terminal (task 1's LiveStateStore::mark_terminal) then deregistering the RunRegistry token on every exit path, and no InternalServerError arm remains.
decisions: Kept live_state.rs's existing API names (record, mark_terminal) rather than the breakdown doc's placeholder names (record_run) since task 1 already implemented them.

On a structural WorkflowError (Err from run_with, not a node failure), fell back to live.get(run_id)'s last recorded snapshot (or an empty TaskContext if none) to satisfy mark_terminal's required snapshot argument; did not add a metadata.failure stamp since docs/data-contract.md explicitly notes that is future work, out of this task's scope.

Repaired both abort_integration.rs and dispatch_integration.rs (the latter not listed in tasks.json's files[] but broken by the same await-to-spawn timing change) by waiting on RunRegistry deregistration instead of treating the 202 trigger response as run-completion.
Split the new budget_from_env_vars unit tests into a nested module importing only the specific function (not `super::*`) to avoid an actix_web::test vs #[test] macro name collision.

3.summary: Added GET /events/{event_id} readback (200 canonical body, 401/404, DB-free) with server-derived status (running/succeeded/cancelled/budget_halted/failed) served from LiveStateStore, backed by a module-local live-run-metadata side table for running runs' workflow_type/created_at.
decisions: Added a private module-level OnceLock<RwLock<HashMap<Uuid,(String,DateTime<Utc>)>>> (live_run_metadata) in http.rs to carry workflow_type/created_at for a still-live run, mirroring the default_budget_from_env 'not an AppState field' pattern — populated right after run_id mint (pre-spawn) and cleared in the spawned task's cleanup after mark_terminal, so AppState gains no new field.

status strings chosen: running | succeeded | cancelled | budget_halted | failed (snake_case), derived in order cancellation -> budget -> failure/node_runs failed -> succeeded; documented as a table in derive_terminal_status's doc comment for the task 6 docs pass to quote.
Malformed/non-UUID path segments and unknown ids both return 404 via the same branch, never 500.

4.summary: Added crates/engine-serve/src/stream.rs (a per-run tokio::sync::broadcast tee, terminal-frame cache for late subscribers, and Lagged-safe recv loop) plus the GET /events/{event_id}/stream SSE endpoint, wired as a third fan-out inside post_events's existing on_progress closure and registered in http.rs's configure/lib.rs.
decisions: Used a two-tier registry (live broadcast::Sender map + a small terminal-frame cache) instead of just dropping the sender on terminal, so a subscriber that connects after a run has already finished still gets a one-shot terminal frame and closes cleanly rather than hanging on a fresh unpublished channel.
Reused http.rs's derive_terminal_status (made pub(crate)) for the SSE terminal frame's status field rather than re-deriving it, keeping one source of truth for terminal-status logic.

Kept the per-run sender registry behind a process-global OnceLock in stream.rs (mirroring http.rs's live_run_metadata/default_budget_from_env precedent) instead of adding it to AppState, per the spec's no-new-AppState-field constraint.
Added futures = { workspace = true } to engine-serve's Cargo.toml (already a workspace dependency) rather than pulling in tokio-stream, and used futures::stream::unfold to build the SSE body.

Dropped a flaky assertion in the HTTP-level integration test that expected to observe an intermediate 'running' frame (inherently racy against the spawned task's first on_progress call); that behavior is instead covered deterministically by stream.rs's unit tests, while the integration test polls until the stream connects and then deterministically asserts the terminal frame (guaranteed since the WaitNode fixture blocks until released after the subscribe is established).

5.summary: Added crates/engine-serve/tests/async_lifecycle.rs, a 5-test in-process actix integration suite proving the block's acceptance criteria: fast 202 under 100ms against a slow node, GET readback transitioning running->terminal, one SSE frame per node transition plus a terminal frame, abort of a spawned run reading back cancelled with the metadata marker, and a run exceeding the default $5 HTTP budget halting with the budget marker.
decisions: Budget-halt test reports cost_usd=10.0 from a fixture node's own output instead of overriding ENGINE_RUN_MAX_COST_USD, because default_budget_from_env() memoizes into a process-global OnceLock — since all tests in this file run in the same test binary (concurrently, in undefined order), any per-test env-var override would race other tests' first call to that memoized default; exceeding the existing $5.0 default via node-reported cost sidesteps the race entirely.

SSE frame-count assertions target only the frames guaranteed to be captured after the stream connects (subscribe() is synchronous inside the handler, so a 200 response guarantees registration) — connecting while the first WaitNode is still blocked and asserting >=4 frames (2nd node's running/success + terminal, plus NodeA's success) avoids flakiness from the documented race where a client can miss frames published before it subscribes (same caveat already called out in http.rs's own stream test).

Used a macro_rules! get_event! helper instead of a generic free function, since test::init_service returns a distinct opaque per-call-site Service type and naming it generically would require adding actix_http as an explicit dependency just for the Request type.
